narratives.text: Atlas quality is deteriorating: test coverage fell from 72% to 63.2% and automated tests from 80.4% to 75.7% since week 8, while defects rose from 6 to 12 (+100%) and rework rate from 8.3% to 12.8%. This may mean more defects reach users and more unplanned rework competes with roadmap work. One possibility worth checking is that falling coverage and automated testing may be letting more defects through, as coverage changes preceded defect changes by 1 week; this is a lagged association, not proof.

On the Data platform, change failure rate rose from 5.4% to 27.1% and rollback rate from 1.1% to 25.9%, while failed deployments went from 0.5 to 6 and incidents from 1 to 5.5 since week 11. This means more failed releases and customer-facing incidents on Data services. One possibility worth checking is whether deployment-related changes are associated with the incident rise: change-attributed incidents went from 50% to 80% in post-incident reviews, though this shift is not statistically significant (p=0.097).

Atlas delivery is slowing: PR review time rose from 10 to 16.5 hours (+65%) and cycle time from 3.2 to 4.5 days since week 8, and lead time from 4.9 to 6.3 days since week 5. Planned work may ship later, putting delivery commitments at risk if the trend continues. Possibilities worth checking are that falling test coverage coincides with longer reviews and that rising rework rate is associated with longer lead time; these are associations between observational series only and do not establish contribution.

Atlas engineering efficiency is declining: average PR size grew from 193 to 245 lines of code (+27%) since week 10, and review latency rose from 3.4 to 4.7 hours (+40%) since week 9. Slower feedback loops may reduce how much Atlas can ship. No validated explanation is available yet; the next step is to profile the Atlas CI pipeline and compare it with codebase and team growth.

On-call pages on the Data platform rose from 7.5 to 14.5 (+93%) since week 10. A rising on-call burden increases fatigue and attrition risk for the engineers supporting Data. No validated explanation is available yet; the next step is to review Data's on-call page volume and how many of those pages are actionable.

Nova's Mobile platform had a one-week disruption in week 11: CI failure rate reached 41 against an expected 7.25, build time 24.1 against 12.35, CI queue time 15.1 against 4.45, on-call pages 25 against 2, and incidents 5 against 0. The impact is limited if it stays isolated, but it would matter if it recurs. Nova / Mobile should confirm a post-incident review captured what happened that week and watch for recurrence.

Titan's build time rose from 12.5 to 15 minutes (+20%) since week 6, a gradual decline in engineering efficiency. Slower feedback loops may reduce how much Titan can ship. No validated explanation is available; the next step is to profile the Titan CI pipeline and compare build time with codebase and team growth.
